evals.prompt: How do I move an order to its next state without changing any of its data?
evals.expected_output: Runs cyoda-help.sh crud --section ENDPOINTS (one section, not the whole topic), answers that a named transition without a data change is PATCH /api/entity/JSON/{id}/{transition} with Content-Type application/merge-patch+json, If-Match: * (or the transactionId) and body {}, warns that a PUT with an empty body is a 400 despite the crud help wording (#684-C), and ends with the source line naming topic, section, SOURCE and VERSION.

files._simulated/help.md: cyoda-help.sh prints SOURCE=instance VERSION=0.8.4 on stderr. `crud --section ENDPOINTS` returns the ENDPOINTS body, including the PATCH /api/entity/{format}/{entityId}/{transition} entry (merge-patch, If-Match required, `{}` is a valid no-op merge 'consistent with PUT-with-empty-body').

assertions.text: Runs `cyoda-help.sh crud --section ENDPOINTS` (or another named crud section) before answering, rather than answering from memory
Reads one section (`--section`), not the whole crud topic
Answer is PATCH /api/entity/JSON/{id}/{transition} with `Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json`, `If-Match: *` (or a transactionId) and body `{}`
Says a PUT with an empty body is rejected (400) even though the crud help implies it's fine, citing #684-C or equivalent
Ends with the source: topic and section plus SOURCE (instance) and version 0.8.4
Synthesises an answer; does not paste the raw help section
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud in its own wording or recommendations

evals.prompt: What does WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED mean? I don't see it in the error list.
evals.expected_output: Runs cyoda-help.sh errors WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED. With no binary and no instance, the helper falls back to the web help mirror; the skill says once that cyoda isn't installed and that the answer comes from the mirror, and says 'next, type /cyoda:setup' to install it. Explains that the index lists 61 of 77 codes and the rest are only in the subtopic list, so the code exists; the workflow version must be a supported MAJOR.MINOR, read from `cyoda help workflows schema-version versions`.

files._simulated/machine.md: `cyoda` is not on PATH. No profile has an endpoint. cyoda-help.sh prints SOURCE=web VERSION=0.8.4 and the whole web page for errors/WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED: HTTP 400, the workflow `version` is not in the supported MAJOR.MINOR range; see `cyoda help workflows schema-version versions`.

assertions.text: Runs `cyoda-help.sh errors WORKFLOW_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` (the per-code page) before answering
Explains that the ERROR CODE INDEX doesn't list every code (61 of 77; the rest only in the subtopic list), so a missing index entry doesn't mean the code doesn't exist
Says the answer comes from the web help mirror because the binary isn't installed, naming the version
Points to `cyoda help workflows schema-version versions` for the supported version instead of stating a version from memory
Any hand-off to a side-effecting skill says 'next, type `/cyoda:setup`' (with a one-line reason) and never says it will invoke or run that skill itself
Does not try to install cyoda itself
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud in its own wording or recommendations

evals.prompt: Can I run Trino SQL reports over my entities? And what's the easiest way to move my app to Cyoda Cloud later?
evals.expected_output: SQL analytics: 'not available in cyoda-go' (help analytics describes an interface cyoda-go doesn't serve), and offers grouped statistics and search, naming crud ENDPOINTS / search ENDPOINTS. Cloud migration: 'That's not covered by this plugin.' and nothing more.

files._simulated/help.md: cyoda-help.sh crud --section ENDPOINTS includes POST /api/entity/stats/{e}/{v}/query (grouped statistics). search --section ENDPOINTS includes POST /api/search/direct/{e}/{v}.

assertions.text: Names or reads the help sections for the alternative it offers (`crud` ENDPOINTS grouped statistics and/or `search` ENDPOINTS)
Says SQL/Trino analytics is not available in cyoda-go
Offers grouped statistics or search as the way to report over entities
Answers the migration question with 'not covered by this plugin' and gives no migration steps
Does not give endpoints or steps from `cyoda help analytics`
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud in its own wording or recommendations

evals.prompt: I'm writing a criteria handler in Kotlin. Exactly which fields does the criteria response need?
evals.expected_output: Gets the schema with cyoda-help.sh cloudevents json piped to jq for processing/EntityCriteriaCalculationResponse.json, reports required requestId and entityId plus matches and the optional reason (2 KiB cap per grpc COMPUTE MEMBER PROTOCOL), and mentions `cyoda help grpc proto` (run with the binary) for stubs.

files._simulated/help.md: cyoda-help.sh cloudevents json prints {schemas:{...}}; schemas["processing/EntityCriteriaCalculationResponse.json"] has required [requestId, entityId] and properties entityId, matches, reason, requestId. `cyoda help grpc proto` prints the .proto text.

assertions.text: Fetches `cyoda help cloudevents json` (via cyoda-help.sh) and selects `processing/EntityCriteriaCalculationResponse.json` with jq rather than listing fields from memory
Lists requestId and entityId as required, plus matches and the optional reason
Points to `cyoda help grpc proto` for generating stubs
Does not point to a GitHub schemas folder or a Cyoda-platform URL
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud in its own wording or recommendations

evals.prompt: The workflows help says my compute node has to declare all of a processor's calculationNodesTags. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: Reads grpc --section "TAG ROUTING": routing is by overlap (one shared tag), random among matching members, empty tags match any member. Says the workflows PROCESSORS wording is wrong (Cyoda/cyoda-go#684 item B) and cites the grpc section as the source.

assertions.text: Reads `cyoda-help.sh grpc --section "TAG ROUTING"` before answering
Says one shared tag is enough (overlap / intersection), not all tags
Says the workflows PROCESSORS wording is wrong and cites #684 item B
Mentions random choice among several matching members, or that empty tags match any member
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud in its own wording or recommendations
